text: Ordered twice this month and both times they were sold out. Everything I wanted was out of stock within an hour.
Bought these as a gift for my sister and the gift wrapping option saved the whole thing.
They run small. The exchange took two emails and the return label arrived the same day, so I sized up half a size from my usual small fit.
Customer service refused my refund for weeks. They refused twice more until I posted publicly, and only then did the refund arrive.

Long overdue project status update for everyone following along at home. The tooling migration finished in March and the firmware branch finally merged after the great rebase, which took three weekends and an amount of coffee I will not disclose. Manufacturing partners rotated again, the anodising vendor is new, and the packaging supplier changed their minimum order so we redesigned the box twice. On logistics, the first pallet cleared customs and the second is out for delivery, though a stock miscount at the warehouse meant a few orders shipped late and we sent a small gift with each delayed unit, plus wrapping for the holiday batch. A handful of buyers asked about an exchange path and a return window, and the store now runs both, with a small restocking note in the FAQ. Firmware wise the debounce logic runs cleaner now, the flash tool got a progress bar, and the configurator exports JSON. Community meetup photos are in the usual thread. Next update lands when the third pallet does, and the spreadsheet of serial numbers is public again for anyone reconciling their order.

The Company's results of operations depend on maintaining adequate inventory across distribution channels, and periods in which popular items are sold out or otherwise out of stock may adversely affect net revenue, customer retention and brand perception. In prior periods the Company has refused refund requests it deemed outside the stated policy, and any change in consumer protection regulation governing a refund obligation could increase costs. The Company relies on a limited number of third party logistics providers, and disruptions at any such provider have previously resulted in inventory being unavailable for sale, delayed replenishment of stock, and cancellation of customer orders. Seasonal demand patterns may cause the Company to carry excess inventory in some periods and insufficient inventory in others, and the Company's forecasts of demand may prove incorrect. Any of the foregoing could materially and adversely affect the Company's business, financial condition and results of operations, and the market price of the common stock could decline. Investors should carefully consider these factors together with the other information contained in this prospectus before deciding to invest.
